en.name: Verba: Voice Translator
en.title: Verba — Voice Translator
en.subtitle: Translate, talk & learn
en.short_description: Translate speech live, practise conversation, and learn words that stick.
en.description:
Verba is a translator you can talk to, and a way to keep what you learn from the conversation.

—— Translate ——

LIVE TRANSLATE
Follow a real conversation as it happens, with speech recognised and translated as people speak.

TRANSLATE
Type or speak a phrase and get it back in the language you need.

TALK
A voice-first mode for when typing is not practical.

—— Learn ——

PRACTICE
Conversational practice, so the language gets used rather than just read.

FLASHCARDS
Spaced repetition brings a word back just before you would have forgotten it, rather than drilling what you already know.

PHRASEBOOK
The phrases you actually need, kept together.

CHAT
A conversational partner to practise against.

—— Built to be used ——

• Natural text-to-speech, so you hear how it should sound
• Material 3 interface with glassmorphic cards
• Notification reminders for your streak and practice, using inexact alarms
• No account needed to start

—— Ads and Premium ——

Verba is free and shows ads through Google AdMob. On iOS you will be asked whether the app may use your device's advertising identifier; you can decline and still use everything. An optional Premium upgrade removes ads.

—— About translation quality ——

Translation and speech recognition are automated and imperfect, especially with accents, background noise, idiom and specialist vocabulary. Do not rely on Verba for medical, legal, financial, safety or immigration matters — use a qualified human interpreter.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing Verba.

Verba is a speech translation and language-learning app. No account is required - the app states "No Account Needed" and every feature is reachable on first launch. It shows ads through Google AdMob and declares NSUserTrackingUsageDescription, so iOS will present an App Tracking Transparency prompt; declining it leaves the app fully usable.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app and step through onboarding. If the App Tracking Transparency prompt appears, either answer is fine - the app works the same.
2. Open Translate and translate a typed phrase, then use the microphone to translate a spoken one.
3. Open Live Translate and speak - the transcript and translation update as you talk. This needs a physical device; a simulator may not provide microphone input.
4. Open Talk for the voice-first mode, and tap playback to hear the text-to-speech.
5. Open Practice and Chat for the conversational modes.
6. Open Flashcards to see the spaced-repetition review queue, and Phrasebook for saved phrases.
7. Open Me - Premium to view the paywall. Ads are removed by the Premium upgrade.
8. Reminders use INEXACT alarms; the app requests no exact-alarm permission.

Privacy:
• Data collected: The phrases you translate, your saved phrasebook entries and your flashcard progress. Advertising identifiers are used for ads if you consent.
• Network: Speech recognition and translation are performed server-side, so audio and text you submit are sent for processing. Ads are served by Google AdMob.
• Location: Not requested and not used.
• Tracking: YES - the app shows ads through Google AdMob and, with your consent via the App Tracking Transparency prompt on iOS, uses your device's advertising identifier for ad relevance and measurement. You can decline, and the app remains fully usable.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
